definitions.explanation: Running away to avoid capture, punishment, or danger. Often used in serious contexts such as crime, war, or political persecution.

examples.japanese: {容疑者|ようぎしゃ}が{逃亡|とうぼう}した。
{戦争|せんそう}から{逃亡|とうぼう}して{隣国|りんごく}に{渡|わた}った。
examples.english: They fled the war and crossed into the neighboring country.

examples.japanese: {逃亡|とうぼう}{生活|せいかつ}を{続|つづ}けていた{犯人|はんにん}が、{十年|じゅうねん}ぶりに{逮捕|たいほ}された。
examples.english: The criminal, who had been living on the run, was arrested for the first time in ten years.

notes:
USAGE NOTES:
{逃亡|とうぼう} implies serious flight — running from the law, escaping persecution, or deserting. It has a heavier tone than {逃|に}げる (to run away) and is common in news reporting.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- から{逃亡|とうぼう}する (to flee from...)
- へ{逃亡|とうぼう}する (to flee to...)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {逃亡|とうぼう}{生活|せいかつ} (life on the run)
- {逃亡|とうぼう}{中|ちゅう} (on the run, at large)
- {逃亡|とうぼう}{者|しゃ} (fugitive)
- {逃亡|とうぼう}を{図|はか}る (to attempt to flee)
- {海外|かいがい}に{逃亡|とうぼう}する (to flee abroad)
